answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol mandates cryptographic stake burning indexed to an agent identity graph. An entity registering multiple identities faces superlinear cost scaling: for each node registered in the network atlas, the burned stake scales quadratically as C(n) = k * n^2, introducing severe economic friction. Identity proofs are locked with quartz clock-drift verification, while consensus messages run through structured sonnet validation proofs. This mathematical barrier makes mass node proliferation exponentially unprofitable for attackers.
